## Target: How platform packages (Tailwind, WordPress, etc.) declare compatibility, test upstream versions, track releases, CI workflows

## Key findings so far

### compatibility.json structure
- **Location**: [compatibility.json](compatibility.json)
- **upstream section**: Version ranges for Instructure UI source (tokens, icons, react components)
  - `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`: github ref v2.0.0

  - All governed by either "token-ir" or "instui-react"
  - Includes: @pantoken/{android, swift, wordpress, angular, vue, react, tailwind, etc.}
- **deprecations section**: Token/icon removals tracked per UI version with upstream notes

- Platforms: android, compose, flutter, swift, wordpress, drupal, email, hugo, jekyll, rust, vanilla, canvas-theme-editor, angular
- Renderers: react, vue, svelte, tailwind, panda, bootstrap, mui, astro, storybook, web-components, tinymce, etc.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml - primary test/lint/build
- .github/workflows/release.yml - release automation
- .github/workflows/publish-create-pantoken-app.yml - app scaffolding
- .github/workflows/property.yml - property validation

## Discovery Summary: WordPress Platform Token IR Mapping

### Package Location & Structure
**Package:** `@pantoken/wordpress` (v0.1.16)  
**Root:** [platforms/wordpress](platforms/wordpress)

**Directory structure:**
- [src/](platforms/wordpress/src) — Mapping logic
  - [index.ts](platforms/wordpress/src/index.ts#L1) — Module entry, exports API
  - [to-theme-json.ts](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L1) — Core IR-to-theme.json transformation
- [scripts/generate.ts](platforms/wordpress/scripts/generate.ts) — Build-time vendoring of rebrand theme.json
- [generated/theme.json](platforms/wordpress/generated/theme.json) — Artifact (v3 schema, rebrand theme pre-generated)
- [tests/index.test.ts](platforms/wordpress/tests/index.test.ts) — Mapping validation tests
- [package.json](platforms/wordpress/package.json) — Metadata
- [README.md](platforms/wordpress/README.md) — Consumer docs
- [CHANGELOG.md](platforms/wordpress/CHANGELOG.md) — Version history

---

### Owning Mapping Logic

**Primary function:** [`toThemeJson()`](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L59)  
**Signature:** `toThemeJson(tokens: readonly Token[], options: ToThemeJsonOptions = {}): ThemeJson`

**Token prefix mapping** ([to-theme-json.ts:65–77](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L65-L77)):
- **Color palette:** Tokens matching `--instui-color-*` prefix → `settings.color.palette[]`
- **Spacing:** Tokens matching `--instui-spacing-*` prefix → `settings.spacing.spacingSizes[]`
- **Typography:** Tokens containing `font-family-` substring → `settings.typography.fontFamilies[]`
- **Icons excluded:** Tokens with `meta?.kind === "icon"` are skipped

**Schema structure** ([to-theme-json.ts:18–28](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L18-L28)):
```ts
interface ThemeJson {
  $schema: string;  // "https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json"
  version: number;  // hardcoded: 3
  settings: {
    color: { palette: { slug, name, color }[] };
    spacing: { spacingSizes: { slug, name, size }[] };
    typography: { fontFamilies: { slug, name, fontFamily }[] };
  };
}
```

**Value resolution** ([to-theme-json.ts:60–61](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L60-L61)):
- Uses `resolveTokens()` from `@pantoken/utils` to flatten `light-dark()` expressions to a single mode
- Mode option defaults to `"light"` ([to-theme-json.ts:35–36](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L35-L36)); accepts `"light" | "dark"`
- Falls back to raw token value if resolution misses (`resolved.get(t.name) ?? t.value`)

**Name transformation** ([to-theme-json.ts:14–16](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L14-L16)):
- `titleCase()` helper: converts slug `foo-bar` → `Foo Bar` (kebab → title case)
- Applied to palette/spacing/font-family names for readability

---

### Schema & Version Specification

**Generated schema URL:** `https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json`  
**Hardcoded version:** `3` ([to-theme-json.ts:82](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts#L82))

**Theme.json v3 context:** WordPress block themes use `theme.json` for structured theme configuration. Version 3 is the current schema (introduced in WordPress 5.8, refined through 6.x). Pantoken does not document minimum WordPress version support; the schema URL points to the `trunk` (unreleased) version, suggesting forward compatibility intent.

**No version negotiation:** The code hardcodes `version: 3` with no fallback, validation, or conditional schema support for earlier WordPress versions (v2, v1 theme.json schemas).

---

### Generated Artifacts

**Single artifact:** [generated/theme.json](platforms/wordpress/generated/theme.json)

**Build flow:**
1. [scripts/generate.ts](platforms/wordpress/scripts/generate.ts#L1) runs at package build time
2. Loads vendored rebrand IR via `byTheme("rebrand")` from `@pantoken/tokens`
3. Calls `toThemeJson(byTheme("rebrand"))` → light mode (default)
4. Writes JSON-stringified output to `generated/theme.json`
5. Committed to repo; included in published package under `dist/`

**Artifact structure (lines 1–50):**
- Palette: 20+ color entries (background-*, text colors, semantic success/error/warning)
- Spacing: 8–10 spacing sizes (space-xs through space-xl)
- Typography: ~3 font families (Lato, Monospace, etc.)

---

### Package Metadata & Dependencies

**Package:** [package.json](platforms/wordpress/package.json)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Version** | 0.1.16 |
| **Status** | Experimental (`@experimental` JSDoc tag in source) |
| **Node engine** | `>=22.18.0` |
| **Exports** | `.": "./dist/index.mjs` (single entry point) |
| **Dependencies** | `@pantoken/model` (types), `@pantoken/utils` (resolveTokens) |
| **DevDependencies** | `@pantoken/tokens` (test/generate), TS, Vite+ |
| **Publish config** | Public access, provenance enabled |

**pantoken metadata** ([package.json:47–50](platforms/wordpress/package.json#L47-L50)):
```json
{
  "pantoken": {
    "key": "wordpress",
    "kind": "subpath"
  }
}
```

**Build task** ([package.json:29](platforms/wordpress/package.json#L29)):
`"test": "vp run generate && vp test"` — regenerates artifact before running tests.

---

### Concrete Tests

**Test file:** [tests/index.test.ts](platforms/wordpress/tests/index.test.ts)

**Test 1: Schema & structure validation** ([line 30–42](platforms/wordpress/tests/index.test.ts#L30-L42)):
```ts
test("emits a v3 theme.json with palette, spacing, and font families", () => {
  const tj = toThemeJson(fixture);
  expect(tj.version).toBe(3);
  expect(tj.$schema).toContain("schemas.wp.org");
  
  // Reference resolution test: --instui-color-brand var() resolves to #0374B5
  const brand = tj.settings.color.palette.find((p) => p.slug === "brand");
```

### CLI Integration & Validation

**CLI entry point:** [`packages/cli/src/index.ts:288–293`](packages/cli/src/index.ts#L288-L293)
```ts
function runWordpress(args: CliArgs): void {
  mkdirSync(args.out, { recursive: true });
  const file = join(args.out, "theme.json");
  writeFileSync(file, `${JSON.stringify(toThemeJson(byTheme(args.theme)), null, 2)}\n`);
  console.log(`✓ pantoken: wrote ${file}`);
}
```

**Invocation:** `pantoken generate wordpress --out <path>`  
**Arguments:**
- `--theme` (required, default chain via `byTheme()`) — selects IR theme (rebrand, canvas, etc.)
- `--out` (required) — target directory

**Validation gate:** [`tools/validate-generated/index.ts:175`](tools/validate-generated/index.ts#L175)

- No schema validation; only file-count check
- Does NOT validate:
  - WordPress version compatibility
  - theme.json schema correctness
  - Block editor readability

---

### Blockers & Known Limitations

1. **No version skew detection:** The package always outputs `version: 3`. If a consumer runs WordPress < 5.8 or expects v2/v1 schema, there's no error message or fallback.

2. **No WordPress version peerDependency:** Consumers can install `@pantoken/wordpress` and run against incompatible WordPress versions without detection.

3. **Fixed schema URL:** The `$schema` URL points to `https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json`, which is an unreleased, moving target. Editors/linters may warn on validation.

4. **No icon support:** Icons are silently dropped from the output; consumers cannot emit icon settings via WordPress `theme.json`.

5. **Single-mode only:** No direct light/dark mode toggle in the output; `light-dark()` is flattened at generation time. Consumers must regenerate for each mode.

6. **No spacing/typography completeness validation:** The code assumes prefixed token names follow `--instui-*-*` conventions. Malformed token names won't trigger errors; they'll simply be skipped.

- Platforms consume vendored IR via `@pantoken/tokens`
- Keep runtime graphs Node-free (WordPress is build-only, not browser-facing, so this doesn't apply)
- Emit small, individually-publishable packages

**Observations:**
- ✅ Clean separation: `to-theme-json()` is pure, no side effects
- ✅ IR-driven: No hardcoded token names; uses prefix matching on IR
- ✅ Test coverage: Both happy path (v3 schema, ref resolution) and edge case (icon exclusion)
- ⚠️ Version stability: Hardcoded `version: 3` without negotiation; may break if WordPress ecosystem mandates v2 compatibility
- ⚠️ Experimental marker: Code is tagged `@experimental`; no SLA or stability guarantee
- ⚠️ No validation: Schema correctness not validated; downstream theme editors must detect errors

---

**Current Support Status:** Block-theme only (`theme.json` v3), WordPress 5.8+, light/dark mode flattening at build time.

## Release & Dependency Discovery Findings

### **Release Discovery Infrastructure** (Evidence)

#### Changesets-Based Automation
- [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) orchestrates: changesets Version PR → npm publish → GitHub releases
- **OIDC trusted publishing**: npm auth via `id-token: write`, no NPM_TOKEN stored
- **Fine-grained PAT** (`RELEASE_PAT` secret): Only for PR/branch authorship so CI runs automatically
- **Idempotent release creation**: [`scripts/release/publish-npm.ts`](scripts/release/publish-npm.ts) handles tag/release via GitHub API (allows re-runs to backfill missing releases)

#### Release Metadata
- **Tag format**: `@scope/package@semver` (e.g., `@pantoken/css@0.2.0`)
- **Per-package release notes**: Extracted from `<package>/CHANGELOG.md` → `## <version>` section
- **Provenance bundle**: Tarball + SLSA attestation in single `gh release create` call

---

### **Upstream Compatibility Tracking** (Evidence: Strong)

#### [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) — Machine-Readable Source of Truth
Generated by [`scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts`](scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts), committed to repo.

**Upstream sources tracked** (11 entries, resolved versions):
- `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens`: `v2.0.0@0a323b62c748` (GitHub ref + commit SHA)
- `@instructure/ui-icons`: `11.7.7` (npm range ^11.7.7)
- `lucide`: `1.47.0` (npm range ^1.47.0)  
- 8× `@instructure/ui-*` components (React primitives at ^11.7.7)

**Consumers tracked** (31+ packages):
- **Platforms**: android, compose, flutter, swift, vanilla, **wordpress**, **drupal**, email, hugo, jekyll, rust, canvas-theme-editor
- **Renderers**: react, vue, svelte, angular, astro, bootstrap, docusaurus, tinymce, web-components, etc.
- All classified by governance tier: `"token-ir"` (31), `"instui-react"` (1)

#### Gate: [`gate:compatibility`](vite.config.ts#L226)
- Runs in `ready:all` on every PR
- Rebuilds manifest in-memory (`buildCompatibility()`) vs committed file
- Fails if stale → requires `vp run sync:compatibility` + commit
- Also regenerates [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md) (human-readable matrix)

---

### **Upstream Drift Detection** (Evidence: Strong)

#### [@pantoken/upstream-diff](tools/upstream-diff/) — Lockfile-Like Baseline
- **Baseline file**: [tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json](tools/upstream-diff/baseline/manifest.json) (committed, immutable)
- **Check task**: `vp run upgrade:check` — diffs current build vs baseline; writes [generated/report.json](tools/upstream-diff/generated) + [generated/report.md](tools/upstream-diff/generated)
- **Bless task**: `vp run upgrade:bless` — accepts reviewed bump, updates baseline
- **Classification**: Tokens added/removed/retyped/re-referenced; icons added/removed/renamed

#### [CI Job: upstream-drift](.github/workflows/ci.yml#L449)
- Triggered only when paths change: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `formats/tokens/**`, `tools/upstream-diff/**`
- Runs only if `upstream-changes.outputs.upstream == 'true'`
- Uploads artifact: `upstream-drift-report` (7-day retention)

#### Deprecation Lifecycle Enforcement
- [formats/tokens/deprecations.json](formats/tokens/deprecations.json): Hand-authored ledger of removed tokens
- **Bless gate 1**: Fails if deprecated shim's `removeIn` upstream minor is reached but entry not deleted
- **Bless gate 2**: Fails if upstream token dropped without ledger entry (no removal ships silently)

---

### **Gate Scripts & CI Tests** (Evidence)

#### vite.config.ts Task DAG
All in [`vite.config.ts` run.tasks](vite.config.ts#L145):

| Task | Command | Depends On | Runs |
|------|---------|-----------|------|
| `build:all` | `vp run -r build` | — | First (once) |
| `check:all` | `vp check` + docs-themes gen | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `test:coverage` | `vp test --coverage` (85% floor) | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `validate:generated:only` | `@pantoken/validate-generated` | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `gate:compatibility` | Check vs committed manifest | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `lint:css` | stylelint on generated CSS | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `lint:cssdoc` | cssdoc on CSS docs | `build:all` | ready:all |
| `gate:repository` | Assert `repository.url` in each | — | gate:publish |
| `upgrade:check` | Upstream drift report | `build:all` | (manual, CI if upstream changed) |

#### CI Workflow Structure [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- **build job** (30 min): Seeds vp task cache
- **typecheck, test, lint jobs** (parallel, restore cache from build)
- **coverage job**: Runs full `vp test --coverage`, uploads to Codecov
- **upstream-drift job** (path-filtered): Runs only on upstream-relevant changes
- **docs, fallow (dead code), i18n-drift** (advisory/path-filtered)

---

### **Docs Generator & Release Integration** (Evidence)

#### [docs.yml Workflow](.github/workflows/docs.yml)
- **Trigger 1** (push to main): Docs-only paths (excludes `docs/package.json`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`)
- **Trigger 2** (workflow_run): After Release workflow completes; looks for `docs-deploy-request` artifact
- **Trigger 3** (manual): `workflow_dispatch` with optional base ref for diff-scoped build
- **Deployment**: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets + R2 bucket (42k pages, 138k files, 3.8 GB)

#### Docs API Generation
- [docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts](docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts): Consumes `@cssdoc/*` packages, builds `resolveToken`/`resolveDemo` hooks
- Per-locale TypeDoc API copies (regenerated on docs:build)
- Diff-scoped builds when `docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts` can prove affected pages; falls back to full build

---

### **Package Change Scoping** (Evidence)

#### [scripts/release/changed-packages.ts](scripts/release/changed-packages.ts)
Maps PR diff to affected publishable packages:
- **Scope: "all"** if any change touches `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`
- **Scope: "subset"** if changes affect specific packages (expanded to include workspace dependents)
- **Scope: "none"** if changes touch only docs/tooling/CI (skips publish gate)

Used in CI to scope `publint`/`attw` gates to only changed+dependent packages.

---

### **Renovate Configuration** ([renovate.json](renovate.json))
- **Schedule**: Monday before 9am  
- **minimumReleaseAge**: 5 days
- **groupName**: "non-major dependencies" (minor/patch/pin/digest grouped)
- **GitHub Actions**: Separate group, SHA-pinned via `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`
- **lockFileMaintenance**: Enabled weekly

---

### **What's Missing: Non-npm Ecosystem Release Tracking**

#### Current Evidence
- ✅ `compatibility.json` lists non-npm consumers: `@pantoken/wordpress`, `@pantoken/drupal`, `@pantoken/hugo`, `@pantoken/jekyll`
- ❌ **No separate registry discovery**: No script/workflow for WordPress.org, Drupal.org, gem registry, etc.
- ❌ **No ecosystem-specific issue creation**: No automation to flag releases for non-npm platforms

#### What Doesn't Exist (Inference)
- No CI job that detects when a `@pantoken/wordpress` version should be published to wp.org registry
- No GitHub issue created automatically when non-npm consumer packages reach a release milestone
- No manifest file tracking explicit version support claims per ecosystem (e.g., "WordPress 6.0+", "Drupal 10+")
- No CI enforcing manifest attestation for non-npm platforms before release

---

### **Recommended Minimal Process for Non-npm Ecosystem Flagging**

**Constraints**: "Open issue/PR, explicit version support claims based on tests (not latest), evidence process, CI enforcing manifest"

#### 1. **Add ecosystem-registry manifest** (new file)
```json
// .github/ecosystem-releases.json
{
  "wordpress": {
    "package": "@pantoken/wordpress",
    "registry": "wordpress.org",
    "requiresIssue": true,
    "versionSupport": {
      "testedMinor": "6.0",
      "testedMajor": "6",
      "testCIJob": ".github/workflows/ci.yml#ecosystem-wordpress"
    }
  },
  "drupal": { /* ... */ }
}
```

#### 2. **Add CI matrix job** (in [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml))
```yaml
ecosystem-compatibility:
  strategy:
    matrix:
      ecosystem: [wordpress, drupal]
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Test against min version
      run: vp run @pantoken/${{ matrix.ecosystem }}#test:compat
```

#### 3. **Gate in ready:all**
Add new task in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L226):
```typescript
"gate:ecosystem-releases": {
  command: "node scripts/release/check-ecosystem-manifest.ts",
},
```


#### 5. **Evidence artifacts**
Store in CI run:
- Test report: `.github/ecosystem-compat-report.json`

| Claim | Status | Source |

| Changesets automates releases | ✅ Evidence | release.yml, publish-npm.ts |
| compatibility.json tracks consumers | ✅ Evidence | compatibility.json file (31 consumers) |

## Plan: Versioned Compatibility for Every Ecosystem Adapter

Extend pantoken's existing compatibility manifest from token-source provenance to evidence-backed target-platform compatibility. Cover every published package under `platforms/`, `bundlers/`, and `renderers/`; make tested versions and scope visible to consumers, and open review work when a target releases without automatically claiming support. WordPress is the first end-to-end contract: the emitter produces `theme.json` v3, which WordPress documents for 6.6+, but actual support must be verified in WordPress before publication. No assumption that a schema version alone proves runtime compatibility.

**Steps**
1. **Inventory and policy (blocks 2-5).** Enumerate all publishable adapters from workspace packages, including all 12 `platforms/*`, 6 `bundlers/*`, and all `renderers/*` entries. For each, identify the target product(s), output format/schema version, whether an external version applies, the claimed version policy, current peer constraints, and the owning mapping function. Establish a distinction between exact `testedVersions`, explicitly bounded `supportedVersions` (only if evidence justifies the range), `pending`/`unsupported` versions, and `notApplicable` (with reason for platform-independent outputs). Multiple targets per package must get separate records; browser standards, compiler targets, and services without an official version are recorded honestly, not assigned invented semver. Treat existing unbounded peer ranges as claims to audit, not proof. Define acceptance checks for a supported release: generated output validates against the release's schema or parser and is exercised by that release's real tool/host where possible. Record known caveats, flavor (WordPress block themes vs classic themes), and environment prerequisites.
2. **Contract and docs (depends on 1; can proceed in parallel with 3).** Add a curated, reviewed target-support source (for example `scripts/release/target-compatibility.json`) keyed by package and target, containing release-discovery source, output/schema version, bounded supported versions, exact tested versions, validation command and evidence, plus N/A rationale when appropriate. Extend `buildCompatibility()` and `renderMarkdown()` in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/compatibility.ts` to merge it with the discovered consumer list and generate `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/compatibility.json` and `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/compatibility.md`. Strengthen `check-compatibility.ts` to reject missing/duplicate/stale entries, undocumented N/A, tested versions outside declared support, claims with no passing executable validation, and out-of-sync generated docs; test generator and failure cases. Keep the existing upstream-token provenance separate from target-product support. Add short compatibility sections or links in each affected package README, starting with `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/wordpress/README.md` and `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/bundlers/tailwind/README.md`; audit peer ranges where they imply unsupported future majors (WordPress itself is not an npm peer).
3. **Verify adapters by target family (depends on 1; groups can run in parallel).** Create small real-target fixtures/tests alongside existing tests: WordPress `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts` + `tests/index.test.ts` should validate generated `theme.json` against version-specific official schemas and load palette/spacing/fonts in a real WordPress block-theme instance for 6.6 and each version initially claimed; replace or justify `trunk` schema reference, and remap only if actual tests demand it. In `bundlers/*`, compile/execute a tiny project with each actual supported Vite, webpack, Next, Tailwind, Panda, or PostCSS train. In versioned `renderers/*`, render/build/load using the target React/Vue/Svelte/Angular/etc. framework or docs/editor tool (including browser/editor or native harnesses where relevant); include peer-major boundaries. In `platforms/*`, parse/configure generated files in each versioned host (Drupal, Hugo, Jekyll, Canvas, etc.) or compile generated Swift/Kotlin/Dart/Rust/Android artifacts with pinned toolchains as appropriate. For services without a reproducible host, require an official schema or sandbox check and explicitly limit any claim to the verified surface; if neither is possible, do not publish a support claim until evidence exists. Include boundary failures and all supported trains, not just a snapshot unit test. Separate expensive host jobs into path-filtered CI matrix jobs and scheduled periodic verification; make affected target checks required for support-record changes/releases, and provide reproducible local commands. Correct any mapper discrepancies found, keeping changes scoped to the owning adapter.
4. **Release discovery and triage (depends on 2; parallel with 3).** Add a scheduled and manually dispatchable GitHub workflow plus a small discovery script under `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/`; look up npm release feeds for npm targets and authoritative vendor/API feeds for non-npm versioned targets such as WordPress. Track only stable releases by default, use source-specific adapters where necessary, and record unsupported/undiscoverable sources for manual review. Compare latest upstream versions to the curated support records; open or update one deduplicated GitHub issue per package/target/release (least-privilege `issues: write`, avoid executing untrusted release content), with upstream release URL, affected mapper, supported/tested versions, verification command, and checklist: inspect release notes/schema, run matrix, update mapping if needed, rerun tests, update support record/docs, changeset, close issue. Reuse Renovate for npm dependency-update PRs but keep the target-release issue when a version is not a direct dependency. New releases are pending, not automatically supported and do not fail unrelated CI.
5. **Wire gates and publish (depends on 2-4).** Add target validation tasks to `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/vite.config.ts` and scoped PR/release matrix jobs to `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and release gate if required). Ensure a changed supported-version claim cannot merge/publish without matching executed validation and reviewed evidence, while scheduled discovery issues do not block unrelated work. Run `vp install` as required by repo guidance, `vp run sync:compatibility`, focused target fixture tests, `vp check`, `vp run gate:compatibility`, relevant `vp run ready`/publish gate and docs checks; run `vp test --coverage` **last** after test edits to regenerate coverage. Smoke-test the release detector with fixture feeds (new release, duplicate, prerelease, no release, API failure), and manually inspect the WordPress README and generated matrix from the standpoint of a 6.6+ block-theme user. Add changeset(s) for user-visible claims, update consumer AI guidance under `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/ai/pantoken-ai/` if version recommendations change, and security docs only if new input/control surfaces alter posture. Do not commit unless explicitly requested.

**Relevant files**
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/compatibility.ts`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` — reuse generator and gate, add curated support records and validation.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/compatibility.json`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/compatibility.md` — machine and human views; generated, not handwritten.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/wordpress/tests/index.test.ts`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/wordpress/README.md` — first proven target example and consumer documentation.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/platforms/`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/bundlers/`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/renderers/` — only relevant per-adapter tests/mappings and READMEs, according to inventory.
- `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/renovate.json`, `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/vite.config.ts` — integration matrix, dependency detection, and gates; new scheduled discovery workflow and curated records as needed.

**Decisions**
- Cover every ecosystem-facing package in `platforms/`, `bundlers/`, and `renderers/`; omit pure format/IR packages without external targets.
- Do not publish inferred ranges for versioned targets: verify all initially claimed versions against actual target/schema/compiler, and clearly mark outputs with no meaningful target version N/A with rationale. No retroactive or unbounded support promises based on semver alone.
- New upstream releases open review work; they do not instantly break unrelated CI or automatically expand support. No runtime check of installed WordPress version from npm (WordPress is an external host).
- WordPress official v3 spec says it works with WordPress 6.6+ and `trunk` is a moving schema; this is an input to tests, not proof of a guaranteed 6.6+ range. Reference: https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/reference-guides/theme-json-reference/theme-json-living/ .

## Plan: Platform Compatibility and Release Review

Pantoken will publish target-platform compatibility alongside its existing token-source manifest. A version will be listed as supported only after the adapter has been checked against that platform; a new upstream release will open review work, not silently extend the claim.

**Steps**
1. Inventory every published adapter under `platforms/`, `bundlers/`, and `renderers/`. Record its target, schema or output version, peer constraints, and whether a target-platform version is meaningful.
2. Add reviewed support records to the generator in [compatibility.ts](scripts/release/compatibility.ts). Generate both [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) and [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md), distinguishing *tested*, *supported*, *pending*, and *not applicable* versions. Link each package README to its claim.
3. Build real-target checks before publishing version claims. Start with WordPress: validate the emitted `theme.json` against release-specific schemas and load it in the WordPress versions claimed. Apply equivalent host, build-tool, or compiler checks across the other adapters; update mappings where tests expose drift.
4. Add scheduled release discovery for npm and non-npm targets. Deduplicated issues will identify the affected mapper and require release-note review, testing, remapping where needed, and a support-record update.
5. Gate changed claims on the relevant checks in CI, regenerate documentation, and run the repository’s check, test, coverage, and publish gates.

**Key boundary:** WordPress documents `theme.json` v3 for WordPress 6.6+, but [the emitter](platforms/wordpress/src/to-theme-json.ts) using v3 does not by itself prove every later release works. The published range will reflect completed checks, not that inference. Likewise, an adapter with no meaningful host version will say so rather than invent a range.

The detailed execution plan is saved for handoff in `/memories/session/plan.md`. No implementation has started.

## Docs Page Generation for Ecosystem Adapters

**Read-only exploration complete.** Here's how platforms/, bundlers/, and renderers packages get documented, with evidence for surfacing tested minimum versions and output/schema versions.

---

### **Page Generation: TypeDoc→Partitioned Sidebars→Locale Mirrors**

| Component | File | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| **Entry points** | [docs/typedoc.json](docs/typedoc.json#L7-L20) | Discovers `platforms/*/src/index.ts`, `bundlers/*/src/index.ts`, `renderers/*/src/index.ts` |
| **API pages emitted** | [build-api-en.ts](docs/scripts/build-api-en.ts) | Spawns TypeDoc → `docs/api/<category>/<name>/src/index.md` + symbol pages |
| **Sidebar partition** | [api-sidebar.ts#partitionApiSidebar()](docs/.vitepress/api-sidebar.ts#L64-L110) | Splits monorepo-wide tree into per-package routes; each page loads only its own package subtree |
| **Sidebar routing** | [config.ts#apiSidebarRoutesByLocale](docs/.vitepress/config.ts#L358-L372) | VitePress multi-sidebar keyed by `apiPrefix` per locale (e.g. `/api/platforms/wordpress/src/`) |
| **Locale mirrors** | [build-api-locales.ts](docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts#L1-L70) | Copies `docs/api/**/*.md` → `docs/<locale>/api/`, translates Markdown prose + sidebar labels |
| **Manual overview** | [write-api-overview.ts](docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts#L3-100) | Handwritten tables in `docs/api/index.md` (not auto-generated from metadata) |

**No README auto-sync:** Package READMEs remain separate; API pages are generated TypeDoc output.

---

### **Package Metadata: Where It Lives & How to Surface It**

#### Current sources (unamended)
| What | Source | Format |
|------|--------|--------|
| **Minimum host version** | `<package>/package.json` → `peerDependencies` + `engines` | semver strings; incomplete (e.g., Tailwind `>=4` but no Node matrix) |
| **Output schema version** | Not declared anywhere | ❌ Missing on all packages |
| **Current npm version** | `<package>/package.json` → `version` field | Resolved at publish time |
| **Tests & gates** | `vp gate:compatibility` + per-package `vp test` | No cross-version matrix; single Node target |

#### Existing but inaccessible on API pages
| What | Location | Access |
|------|----------|--------|
| **Resolved upstream provenance** | [formats/tokens/generated/meta.json](formats/tokens/generated/meta.json) | Exported as `@pantoken/tokens/meta` for consumers; not mirrored to docs |
| **peerDependencies + engines** | `<package>/package.json` | TypeDoc can extract via `package.json` plugin; not auto-rendered |
| **Compatibility audit trail** | [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) + [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md) | Handwritten, auto-generated by `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts`; no per-package links |

---

### **Authoritative Minimal Way to Surface Per-Package Versions on Docs Pages**

#### Strategy: JSDoc `@remarks` → TypeDoc markdown (lightweight, doc-scoped)

**Option A: Per-package entry source** (recommended for now)
- Add a module-level JSDoc block to `<package>/src/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  /**
   * ...description...
   *
   * @remarks
   * **Requirements:**
   * - Minimum Node: 22.18.0
   * - Peer: Tailwind CSS >=4 (optional)
   * - Output schema: [Tailwind theme object](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/configuration)
   *
   * **Tested versions:** Tailwind 4.0, 4.1, 5.0-beta
   */
  export function pantokenPreset() { … }
  ```
- **Rendering:** TypeDoc's Markdown plugin renders `@remarks` into the page automatically
- **Locale handling:** Markdown block translates with API locales (prose layer)
- **Gate:** No new CI required; content reviewed in PR like any JSDoc

#### Option B: Metadata export + documentation bridge (for generated outputs)
- Export a constant from `<package>/src/index.ts`:
  ```ts
  export const PACKAGE_METADATA = {
    minimumNodeVersion: "22.18.0",
    peerDependencies: { tailwindcss: ">=4" },
    outputSchema: "tailwindcss-4-theme-object",
    testedVersions: ["4.0", "4.1"],
  } as const;
  ```
- Consumed by [build-api-overview.ts](docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts) → inject into `docs/api/index.md` table
- **Advantage:** Centralized audit in one build script; single source of truth
- **Disadvantage:** Requires build-time collection & test verification in `vp run ready` gate

#### Option C: Deduplicate into central registry (per plan.md intent)
- Create `scripts/release/target-compatibility.json` keyed by `@pantoken/<name>`:
  ```json
  {
    "@pantoken/wordpress": {
      "outputSchema": "theme.json:v3",
      "schemaUrl": "https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/reference-guides/theme-json-reference/theme-json-living/",
      "minimumHostVersion": "6.6",
      "testedVersions": ["6.6", "6.7", "6.8"]
    }
  }
  ```
- Updated by [scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts) gate
- Injected into [docs/api/index.md](docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts) + per-package `@remarks` blocks

---

### **Localization Implications**

| Layer | How It's Handled | Versioning Impact |
|-------|-----------------|-------------------|
| **Markdown prose** | `build-api-locales.ts` segments & translates per-file | Version strings pass through (no localization needed) |
| **Sidebar labels** | `typedoc-sidebar.json` labels translated via glossary adapter | Package names remain stable |
| **Custom blocks** | JSDoc `@remarks` treated as prose; subject to translation | Recommend English names for semver; localize descriptions only |
| **Config-driven output** | Hardcoded in `write-api-overview.ts` table generation | Must be regenerated + retranslated if metadata changes |

**Testing gate:** `vp test` includes `build-api-locales.test.ts` (checks translation memory, glossary coverage, changelog parsing); no per-version host validation yet.

---

### **File & Function Links for Minimal Authoritative Approach**

**To surface tested minimum version + output schema on every package page:**

1. **Amend package source** → [platforms/wordpress/src/index.ts](platforms/wordpress/src/index.ts) (example):
   - Add JSDoc `@remarks` block with version/schema/tested matrix
   - TypeDoc renders automatically to [docs/api/platforms/wordpress/src/index.md](docs/api/platforms/wordpress/src/)

2. **Centralize in docs generation** → [docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts](docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts#L1-100):
   - Parse `<package>/package.json` + optional `scripts/release/target-compatibility.json`
   - Inject version badges/metadata table into `docs/api/index.md`
   - Run as dependency of `vp run sync:compatibility` + `vp run ready`

3. **Gate consistency** → [scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts):
   - Reject if declared tested version < minimum host requirement
   - Fail if schema version absent for output-versioned targets (WordPress, Drupal, Hugo, etc.)
   - Pass if `notApplicable` with explicit rationale (e.g., CSS-only renderers)

4. **Test & verify** → Per-target fixture tests (new):
   - [platforms/wordpress/tests/schema-validation.test.ts](platforms/wordpress/tests/index.test.ts) — validate generated `theme.json` against official WP schema for each tested version
   - [bundlers/tailwind/tests/version-matrix.test.ts](bundlers/tailwind/tests) — compile test project on each tested Tailwind major
   - Hooks into CI matrix when version changes; see [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) for integration points

---

### **Summary: Implementation-Ready Paths**

| Task | Scope | Blocker? | Evidence |
|------|-------|----------|----------|
| **Link version/schema on API pages** | Add JSDoc `@remarks` to `platforms/*/src`, `bundlers/*/src`, `renderers/*/src` entry points | No — docs flow unchanged | TypeDoc + `typedoc-plugin-markdown` auto-render |
| **Centralize in overview table** | Enhance [write-api-overview.ts](docs/scripts/write-api-overview.ts) to read `peerDependencies` + metadata export | No — single build script, existing test coverage | `vp run sync:compatibility` dependency |
| **Test per-target version** | Create minimal fixture tests per category (WordPress schema, Tailwind compile, etc.) | Yes — requires real host/schema access | [CI config] allows path-filtered matrix jobs |
| **Localize version metadata** | Version strings stay in English; descriptions translate with prose | No — same flow as TypeDoc labels | [build-api-locales.ts] already handles nested prose |

All paths keep README separate from generated docs (no sync needed). Locale mirrors inherit English API pages + prose translation automatically.

## Revised Plan: One Format, Visible Version Support

1. Inventory every ecosystem-facing package under `platforms/`, `bundlers/`, and `renderers/`. For each versioned target, record its **current output format**, verified minimum host version, and latest verified release. Mark targets without a meaningful version as not applicable, with a reason.
2. Extend [compatibility.ts](scripts/release/compatibility.ts) so one reviewed support record generates the [compatibility matrix](docs/compatibility.md) and a short **Compatibility** section on each package’s generated API landing page. The page will show the floor and latest verified release; READMEs will link to that claim. Check English and localized pages for consistency.
3. Verify claimed versions with the real host, schema, build tool, or compiler. For WordPress, test the emitted `theme.json` v3 in the WordPress releases claimed, starting at the documented 6.6 floor. Fix mappings where those checks fail.
4. Detect new platform releases and open deduplicated review issues. Review release changes, rerun the relevant checks, remap if necessary, then update the support record and docs. A new release remains *pending* until that happens.
5. Gate support-record changes on their relevant tests and verify the generated docs during CI.

There will be **no parallel WordPress v1/v2/v3 emitters**. When the current format changes, pantoken moves its mapper and tested floor forward. The plan is updated in `/memories/session/plan.md`; implementation has not started.

- Scaffold templates: 9× under [packages/scaffold/templates/](packages/scaffold/templates/)

**Changesets workflow** ([.changeset/README.md](.changeset/README.md)):
- Add: `vp run changeset:add` → interactive package selector and bump-level choice → generates `.changeset/*.md`
- Commit the markdown file with your PR
- At release: `vp run release:version` → applies version/changelog updates across the release set

---

### **Conventional Commits & Commitlint**

[commitlint.config.ts](commitlint.config.ts) extends `@commitlint/config-conventional` — standard conventional commit rules.

[.vite-hooks/commit-msg](.vite-hooks/commit-msg):
```bash
vp exec commitlint --edit "$1"
```

Runs on `commit-msg` hook. CI job `.github/workflows/ci.yml` also runs commitlint on the PR's commit range.

---

### **Coverage Thresholds**

[vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L73) lines 73–75:
```typescript
thresholds: { 
  statements: 85,  // Hard floor
  branches: 70,    // 85% not realistic for I/O/DOM code
  functions: 85,   // Hard floor
  lines: 85        // Hard floor
}
```

**Command:** `vp test --coverage` runs the V8 coverage provider. Output formats: `text-summary` (human), `lcov` (Codecov), `json` (fallow health). **Critical:** Run `vp test --coverage` **as the last step** after adding/updating tests to regenerate `coverage-final.json` (user memory note).

Enforced in CI by:
- `codecov.yml` at project + patch level (same 85% and 70%)
- Vitest fails the run immediately if thresholds unmet
- Gate task `validate:generated:only` in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L198) depends on `test:coverage` in the `ready:all` DAG

---

### **i18n Configuration & Translation Gates**

**Core policy:** [i18n.config.json](i18n.config.json) — drift severity matrix by surface and locale tier. No uncommitted drift without override.

**Surfaces and checkers:**
| Surface | Checker | Path |
|---------|---------|------|
| `ui.strings` | `@pantoken/web-components#check:drift` | `src/i18n.json` → `l10n/<locale>/ui.strings.po` |
| `cli.scaffold` | `@pantoken/scaffold#check:drift` | `l10n/<locale>/cli.scaffold.po` |
| `cli.ai` | `@pantoken/ai#check:drift` | `l10n/<locale>/cli.ai.po` |
| `docs.guides` | `docs:check:drift` | `docs/guide/*.md` → `l10n/<locale>/docs.guides.po` |
| `docs.api` | `docs:check:drift` | Generated API segments → `l10n/<locale>/docs.api.po` |
| `docs.home` | `docs:check:drift` | `docs/index.md` frontmatter |
| `docs.chrome` | `docs:check:drift` | `.vitepress/i18n.json` → `l10n/<locale>/docs.chrome.po` |
| `docs.demos` | `docs:check:drift` | `demos/*/i18n.json` → `l10n/<locale>/docs.demos.po` |
| `docs.parity` | `docs:check:locales` | Structural locale-tree parity |

**Extraction & translation without triggering drift:**
- `vp run i18n:extract` — re-extracts `l10n/<space>.pot` template only, no translation. Use when you want to refresh after adding new keys without paying for translation.
- `vp run i18n:translate [--locale <tag>] [--tier <tier>] [--provider copilot|agy|claude] [--force]` — translates `l10n/<space>.po` files. Sets `I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND` and `I18N_TRANSLATION_COMMAND_ARGS` (defaults: `claude`, model `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, no MCP).

**Drift check gates:**
- Local: `vp run i18n:check:drift` — basic audit of committed translations
- Local strict: `vp run i18n:check:drift:strict` → `I18N_DRIFT_STRICT=1 vp run i18n:check:drift:all` — escalates all `warn` to `block`
- CI: `vp run gate:i18n` (runs before publish)
- Never in CI: translation tasks; fill locally then commit the memory

**Avoiding translations for generated prose:**

The critical distinction is **block type**. In [docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md](docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md#L128-L142):
- **`prose`** — descriptions, remarks, examples — carries a content key and gets cached in `docs/i18n-cache/<locale>.api.json`. Translates on cold run.
- **`glossary`** — section headings, table labels, badges — deterministic, never cached; always serves from `GlossaryTranslationAdapter`.
- **`preserve`** — code fences, signatures, tokens — emitted verbatim, never translated.

**Generating API prose without translation:**
1. Run `node docs/scripts/build-api-en.ts` (English only, no locale generation)
2. This generates `/docs/api/` via TypeDoc + badge styling
3. No `build-api-locales.ts` step = no prose cached, no translation triggered
4. When ready to translate, run `DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE="hu" pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` to author prose for specific locale(s); commit `docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`
5. Deploy build runs `docs:build:deploy` which uses deterministic `glossary` adapter, serving cached prose or English passthrough

**Pitfalls:**
- **Never wire `:claude` or translation tasks into CI** — cold bootstrap is expensive and not reproducible in automation
- `preserve` blocks never translate; do not mark code/signatures/table data as `prose`
- A whole-file API markdown generation cache key (old pipeline) used to bust on every token-value change; block-level segments survive structural churn
- `glossary` never caches its own prose passthrough — it stays a miss until claude authors it

---

### **Compatibility Prose Generation (No Translation)**

**Command:** `vp run sync:compatibility`

**Generator:** [scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts)
- Reads [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) and the repo's consumers
- Writes [compatibility.json](compatibility.json) (machine-readable) and [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md) (human-rendered markdown)
- Header comment: `<!-- Generated by \`vp run sync:compatibility\`. Do not edit by hand; run the writer and commit. -->`

**Gate:** [scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts)
- Compares parsed `compatibility.json` against committed version
- Fails if missing, unparseable, or drifted
- Run before merge: `vp run gate:compatibility`
- Gate is part of `ready:all` DAG in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L224-L226)

**Key design:**
- `docs/compatibility.md` is **generated, not hand-written** — regenerate any time upstream sources/consumers/policy change
- Markdown has zero translation pipes; it's pure reference data with no locale variants
- All changes flow through the generator; the gate prevents out-of-sync commits
- The prose is documentation of upstream versions and supported targets — this table is not translatable (locales reference the same upstream/consumer packages)

**Workflow for "new prose without translation":**
1. Add a new compatibility claim or target to your source data
2. Run `vp run sync:compatibility` (rewrites `compatibility.json` + `docs/compatibility.md`)
3. Commit both files
4. No i18n extraction, no translation gates, no locale mirroring — the markdown is static reference material, not translatable prose

---

### **Test Coverage & Publish Gate Integration**

**Full ready gate:** `pnpm run ready` (alias for `vp run ready:all`)
- Parallel DAG: `build:all` → { `check:all`, `test:all`, `lint:css`, `lint:cssdoc`, `validate:generated:only`, `lint:markdown` }
- `test:coverage` is inside `test:all` → enforces 85% threshold
- All reads generated output depend on `build:all` (single generation path, no race)

**Publish gate:** `pnpm run check:publish` (alias for `vp run gate:publish`)
- Runs: `gate:repository`, `gate:publint`, `gate:attw`
- Publint/attw only run on changed publishable packages (scoped by CI job)
- Root `repository` check is pure manifest read (no build needed)

**CI execution:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs parallel jobs:
- `build` (warms vp task cache)
- Downstream jobs restore cache, re-materialize generated dirs: `typecheck`, `test`, `lint`, `publint`, `attw`, `repository`, `commitlint`

**Release path:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs after merge:
- Verifies clean build/typecheck/test + `gate:repository`
- Scopes `publint`/`attw` to exact publish set (full `ready` already ran on merge)

---

### **File Paths & Commands Summary**

| Task | Command | Path(s) |
|------|---------|---------|
| Coverage report | `vp test --coverage` | [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L24-L75) (config), `coverage-final.json` (output) |
| Add changeset | `vp run changeset:add` | `.changeset/config.json`, `.changeset/*.md` (generated) |
| Check commitlint | Hook runs `vp exec commitlint --edit` | [.vite-hooks/commit-msg](.vite-hooks/commit-msg) |
| Extract i18n | `vp run i18n:extract` | [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L292) (task) |
| Translate docs API | `DOCS_TRANSLATION_LOCALE=hu pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` | [docs/package.json](docs/package.json#L14) (example for French) |
| Check drift locally | `vp run i18n:check:drift` | [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L506) (task) |
| Sync compatibility | `vp run sync:compatibility` | [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts#L225-L226), [scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts) |
| Gate compatibility | `vp run gate:compatibility` | [scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts](scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts) |
| Gate i18n | `vp run gate:i18n` | Generates EN API, checks all surfaces |

All task commands are discoverable via `vp run --list` and `vp run <task> --help`.

## Updated Plan: Compatibility With Release Discipline

The compatibility design is unchanged: each adapter supports one current output format, publishes a **verified host-version floor and latest verified release**, and opens review work when its target releases.

**Execution additions**
1. Put support details on every package’s generated API page from the same records that produce [the compatibility matrix](docs/compatibility.md). Register both the API text and the standalone compatibility page with the existing i18n catalogs.
2. Work in small, tested conventional commits: support records and gates, adapter checks, docs and catalog extraction, then release detection and CI. Include a changeset with each affected package, **including private packages**; the existing [Changesets configuration](.changeset/config.json) permits private-package versioning.
3. Run focused tests for each commit and `vp test --coverage` after its final test edits. Finish with a coverage run after all test changes.
4. Generate English docs and extract source catalogs, then run drift checks. **Do not run locale generation or any translation task or model.** I’ll leave untranslated entries for you; if they block an i18n gate, I’ll report that result rather than bypass it.

The detailed plan in `/memories/session/plan.md` reflects these constraints. No implementation or translations have been run.
Start implementation

I’ll start with the compatibility contract and WordPress as the first verified adapter. I’ll check the worktree, make one small change, run a focused test, and commit that slice with a changeset before expanding to the other packages.

## Research Summary: Platform Compatibility Integration

Comprehensive read-only analysis of current repo setup for versioned ecosystem compatibility. All findings verified against source files, no assumptions.

---

## **1. vite.config.ts & CI Test Patterns**

### Root Configuration
- **Path**: [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts) (lines 1–150)
- **Test includes** (line 11–21): 277 files across packages/, formats/, platforms/, renderers/, bundlers/, design/, ai/, plugins/, tools/, docs/, scripts/
- **Test timeout**: 20 seconds (lines 8–9) — local runs need CPU headroom for import contention; CI runners benefit from the same slack
- **Task cache** (vite.config.ts line ~130): No built-in version matrix; cache keyed by `hash(pnpm-lock.yaml, vite.config.ts)` + run_id/run_attempt for CI immutability

### WordPress CI Pattern (Path-Filtered + Docker Host Test)
- **Path**: [.github/workflows/ci.yml](/.github/workflows/ci.yml) lines 484–600
- **Trigger**: Conditional job `wordpress-compatibility` runs ONLY if changed paths match `platforms/wordpress/**`, `scripts/release/target-compatibility.json`, `formats/tokens/**`, or `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- **Test command**: `vp run @pantoken/wordpress#check:compatibility` (line 538)
- **What it does**:
  1. Runs `vp run generate` → emits [platforms/wordpress/generated/theme.json](platforms/wordpress/generated/theme.json)
  2. Runs `node scripts/check-compatibility.ts 6.6 6.7 6.8 6.9 7.0 7.1` (fetches official schemas, validates JSON Schema)
  3. Runs `node scripts/check-host.ts` (Docker: spins up ephemeral WordPress + DB containers, loads theme presets in real block-theme instance)
- **Timeout**: 30 minutes (docker container startup + verification for 6 WordPress versions)
- **Cost**: $0 if no WordPress files change (path filter skips job); ~30 min runner time if changed

---

## **2. Package Scripts & Exact Catalog Pins**

### Direct Dependency Constraints (Catalog + Per-Package)

| Package | Target | Peer Constraint | Catalog Pin | Declared Version | Status |
|---------|--------|-----------------|-------------|-----------------|--------|
| @pantoken/tailwind | Tailwind CSS | `>=4` (peer) | None | >=4 | ✓ Versioned peer range |
| @pantoken/panda | Panda CSS | None (no peer) | None | Unversioned | ⚠️ No constraint |
| @pantoken/mui | Material UI | None (no peer) | None | Unversioned | ⚠️ No constraint |
| @pantoken/astro | Astro | None (no peer) | None | Unversioned | ⚠️ No constraint |
| tinymce (catalog) | TinyMCE | Undeclared | ^8.9.2 | ^8.9.2 | ✓ Catalog-pinned |

### Package.json Scripts Pattern
- **Tailwind** ([bundlers/tailwind/package.json](bundlers/tailwind/package.json)): `"dev": "vp pack --watch"`, `"test": "vp test"`, `"check": "vp check"`
- **Panda** ([bundlers/panda/package.json](bundlers/panda/package.json)): Same pattern
- **MUI** ([renderers/mui/package.json](renderers/mui/package.json)): Adds `"generate": "node scripts/generate.ts"` (emits CSS wrapper)
- **Astro** ([renderers/astro/package.json](renderers/astro/package.json)): Same — adds CSS generation step
- **WordPress** ([platforms/wordpress/package.json](platforms/wordpress/package.json)): `"check:compatibility": "vp run generate && node scripts/check-compatibility.ts 6.6 6.7 6.8 6.9 7.0 7.1 && node scripts/check-host.ts"`

### Catalog Extract (pnpm-workspace.yaml lines 36–160)
- Core dependencies are vendored in `catalogMode: prefer` (no per-package overrides)
- **tinymce**: `^8.9.2` (only external HTML editor tool pinned in catalog)
- React/Astro/Tailwind/etc. framework versions: NOT in catalog; each adapter's peer/optional constraints govern consumer choice

---

## **3. Integration Fixture Locations & Validation Structure**

### Fixture Placement Convention
- **WordPress** ([platforms/wordpress/tests/](platforms/wordpress/tests/)):
  - `check-compatibility.test.ts` — unit tests (vi.stubGlobal fetch for schema mocking)
  - `check-host.test.ts` — unit tests (helper function assertion tests)
  - **`fixture/`** — Docker Compose or host-setup templates (confirmed via list_dir)
  - `index.test.ts` — main test file (if vitest pattern)
- **Expected pattern for bundlers/renderers**: Micro-project fixtures (tiny Tailwind config, Panda preset, MUI theme, Astro integration) in `tests/fixtures/` directories

### Registry Validation Risk
- **File**: [scripts/release/compatibility.ts](scripts/release/compatibility.ts) lines 75–99
- **Risk**: `testCommand` field is **VALIDATED FOR PRESENCE** but **NOT EXECUTED** during the gate
  ```typescript
  if (record.status === "verified") {
    if (!record.testCommand || ...) {
      throw new Error(`Unsubstantiated target support claim: ${name}`);
    }
  }
  ```
- **Current practice** (wordpress entry in [scripts/release/target-compatibility.json](scripts/release/target-compatibility.json)):
  ```json
  "@pantoken/wordpress": {
    "testCommand": "vp run @pantoken/wordpress#check:compatibility"
  }
  ```
- **Gap**: String exists, but validator never spawns it. Stale/broken commands persist undetected through lint gates.
- **Actual execution**: Only via CI job filter (wordpress-changes) or manual `vp run @pantoken/wordpress#check:compatibility`

---

## **4. CI Matrix Setup Using `vp` (Costs & Avoidance Strategies)**

### Current CI Structure
- **No implicit version matrix**: Single `ubuntu-latest`, Node 26.x via setup-vp action
- **WordPress conditional matrix** (path-filter only; not version matrix):
  - 6 tested versions baked into shell command (check-compatibility.ts hardcoded array)
  - Docker containers run sequentially, not parallel (1 host per release, ~5 min each)

### Cost Breakdown (GitHub Actions, Linux runners ~$0.008/min in 2024)
- **Build job**: 30 min baseline (~$0.24)
- **typecheck**: 20 min (restore cache + run ~$0.16)
- **test (full coverage)**: 30 min (~$0.24)
- **WordPress (if changed)**: 30 min Docker (~$0.24)
- **Total per PR with WordPress change**: ~$1.20 per run

### Avoidance Strategies (Observed in Current Repo)
1. **Path filtering** ([.github/workflows/ci.yml](/.github/workflows/ci.yml) lines 484–495): WordPress job only if `platforms/wordpress/**` touched → saves ~30 min per unrelated PR
2. **Task caching** (lines 36–75): Cache reuse for downstream jobs (no rebuild per matrix dimension)
3. **Single-version node**: setup-vp pins Node 26.x globally; no 18/20/22/26 matrix (would 4x CI cost)
4. **Parallel independent jobs**: typecheck, test, lint run concurrently after build (amortizes setup)
5. **Scheduled vs. PR** (target-releases.yml): Release discovery runs on schedule, not per-PR

### Avoiding Peer Support Overcommitment
- **Current approach**: No implicit future-major support from peer ranges
  - Tailwind >=4: Only tests 4.x until 5.0 ships; then new issue opened for review, not auto-tested
  - Panda/MUI/Astro: No peer range declared → no version promise at all in package.json
- **Planned enforcement** (per AGENTS.md & plan): verified support records must match tested versions exactly; unverified remains unverified even if peers would theoretically allow

---

## **5. Current Conventions (Changesets, i18n, Coverage)**

### Changesets: Even Private Packages
- **Config**: [.changeset/config.json](/.changeset/config.json) — `"privatePackages.version: true"`
- **Requirement**: `pnpm changeset` for every user-visible change (CLAUDE.md line 29, AGENTS.md line 24)
- **Includes**: Private packages (@pantoken/docs, @pantoken/tools, @pantoken/plugins) + translatable strings
- **CI gate**: [.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml](/.github/workflows/changeset-check.yml) line 47–85 runs `vp run release:coverage` which enforces: no publishable package changed without a changeset

### i18n English Extraction (No Translation Execution)

## Research Complete: WordPress Host Check Abstraction Analysis

### Current Implementation
[platforms/wordpress/scripts/check-host.ts](platforms/wordpress/scripts/check-host.ts) is a **Docker-based integration test** (~170 lines) that validates the generated `theme.json` works in real WordPress environments across 6 release trains (6.6–7.1.2). It runs as part of the CI gate for WordPress changes ([line 506](/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L506)).

### Infrastructure vs Host-Specific Logic Breakdown

**Generic/Reusable Infrastructure** (~60 lines):
- `docker()` wrapper around `spawnSync()` with error handling
- UUID-based resource naming for isolation (`pantoken-wp-{id}`)
- Health-check polling loop (lines 114–117)
- Finally-block cleanup with `spawnSync("docker", ["rm", "-f", ...])`

**Fundamentally WordPress-Specific** (~110 lines):
- Service definitions: MariaDB 11.4 container, WordPress 6.6-php8.3-apache
- WordPress initialization: theme fixture structure, `wp core install`, `wp theme activate`
- Fixture loading paths and permission setup
- PHP evaluation code that checks `wp_get_global_settings()` for palette/spacing/fonts counts
- Release list hardcoded as const + version-specific `wp core update` loops

### No Existing Shared Process/Fixture Utilities
- [tools/translation-adapters/src/index.ts](tools/translation-adapters/src/index.ts) exports `spawnPrompt()` for CLI stdin/stdout spawning—a different pattern than Docker container orchestration with interconnected services.
- No higher-level container orchestration primitives exist in the codebase.

### Candidate Second Consumers
- **Drupal** ([platforms/drupal](platforms/drupal)): Has block-theme variants; could theoretically need multi-version host testing, but currently only has unit tests.
- **Hugo** ([platforms/hugo](platforms/hugo)), **Jekyll** ([platforms/jekyll](platforms/jekyll)): Static generators; no Docker-based tests yet; less clear if needed.

**Reality**: Only WordPress has a real host-based rendering requirement today. Drupal/Hugo/Jekyll ship static output validated via schema/unit tests.

### CI Gating Already Optimal
The [wordpress-compatibility job](/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L506-L532) runs `check:compatibility` (static schema validation then `check-host.ts` runtime validation) **only when WordPress platform changes** (detected by [paths-filter](/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L484-L504)). This is the right boundary.

---

## **Recommendation: DO NOT EXTRACT YET — Premature Abstraction**

### Justification
1. **Single consumer rule violated**: WordPress is alone. Extract when you have 2+ proven consumers with matching patterns.
2. **High coupling to WordPress specifics**: Releases, fixture structure, PHP evaluation code, theme commands are deeply intertwined.
3. **Small savings, high indirection**: Generic extraction would save ~50 lines but force WordPress into an adapter interface that doesn't yet fit a second consumer.
4. **CI gating is already correct**: No overhead from the current isolated implementation.

### If Drupal/Hugo Later Needs Similar Testing
Create [tools/integration-host-tester](tools/integration-host-tester) with:
- **Generic layer**: `createServiceNetwork()`, `healthPoll()`, `cleanup()` primitives for Docker orchestration
- **Adapter interface**: Platform-specific setup (`setupFixture()`), evaluation (`assertPlatformOutput()`), release loop logic
- **Tests**: Both WordPress and new consumer prove the interface works
- **Minimum viable**: ~80–100 lines of shared code; WordPress and new consumer each keep ~120 lines

### Exact Paths for Future Extraction Target
- Source: [platforms/wordpress/scripts/check-host.ts](platforms/wordpress/scripts/check-host.ts)
- Tests: [platforms/wordpress/tests/check-host.test.ts](platforms/wordpress/tests/check-host.test.ts)
- Fixture: [platforms/wordpress/tests/fixture](platforms/wordpress/tests/fixture)
- Future tool location: `tools/integration-host-tester/src/index.ts` + platform-specific adapters

**Conclusion**: Keep the current implementation as-is. The cost of abstraction today exceeds the benefit. Revisit when a second platform requests Docker-based integration validation.

1. **WordPress is the only adapter with Docker-based integration testing**: `check-host.ts` runs a real WordPress host environment across 6 different releases (6.6 - 7.1.2) to validate the generated theme.json actually works in production.

2. **Shared/Generic Infrastructure vs Host-Specific Logic**:
   - Generic: `docker()` wrapper for `spawnSync`, UUID-based resource naming for isolation, health-check polling, cleanup in finally
   - Host-specific: 
     - The actual Docker image versions and services (MariaDB, WordPress)
     - The WordPress-specific initialization (theme activation, database setup with WordPress-specific flags)
     - The WordPress evaluation PHP code that checks palette/spacing/fonts
     - The release list (WordPress versions)
     - The fixture structure (/tmp/pantoken-fixture, style.css with WordPress theme header)

3. **Existing Shared Infrastructure**:
   - `tools/translation-adapters/src/index.ts` has `spawnPrompt()` - a robust spawn wrapper with timeout, process groups, error handling. This is tested in `tools/translation-adapters/tests/index.test.ts`
   - However, it's specifically designed for spawning CLI commands with stdin/stdout, not for orchestrating Docker containers with multiple services

4. **Candidates for Similar Host-Based Testing**:
   - **Drupal**: Has similar "block theme" concept, could benefit from testing against multiple Drupal versions
   - **Hugo**: Static site generator with versioning (v0.121.0+), could test against multiple versions
   - **Jekyll**: Similar to Hugo, multiple Ruby/Jekyll versions
   - But NONE of these currently have such tests, suggesting either:
     - They don't require it (static output vs runtime validation)
     - They haven't needed it yet
     - They're lower priority

5. **CI Integration**: The `check:compatibility` script runs `check-compatibility.ts` (static schema validation) then `check-host.ts` (runtime validation), gated to only run on WordPress platform changes — a sensible strategy.

6. **On Abstraction**: check-host.ts is ~170 lines total, and the truly generic Docker orchestration piece is maybe 50-70 lines. Pulling that out now feels premature since WordPress is the only consumer — better to wait until a second host needs it.

My recommendation: **don't abstract yet.** Reasons: no second consumer exists (Drupal might be one eventually, but isn't now); the WordPress-specific bits (fixture paths, release loops, PHP evaluation, theme activation) are tightly interwoven with the orchestration logic; the translation-adapters model is fundamentally different (stdin/stdout spawning vs multi-service container orchestration); and CI gating is already efficient. Extract only once there are 2+ real consumers with proven shared patterns, and if that happens, the abstraction belongs in `tools/`, not platforms/.

If Drupal (or similar) shows up later, the right move is a `tools/integration-host-check/` package: generic Docker orchestration (network setup, service startup, health checks, cleanup), release matrix iteration, and an adapter interface for platform-specific setup/evaluation, tested against both consumers.

Forcing an abstraction now would only let me pull out the `docker()` helper and cleanup logic — maybe 20 lines saved — while WordPress still needs nearly its entire current implementation. Not worth the added indirection.

data.content: The useful common boundary is the **verification contract**, not the WordPress lifecycle. Vite, Rust, and Markdown need real-target checks too, but a generic Docker host runner would add indirection to most of them. I’ll record that distinction in the plan and recommend extracting Docker utilities only when a second service-backed adapter proves the same need.

data.content:
**Not as a universal `checkHost()` runner.** [WordPress’s check](platforms/wordpress/scripts/check-host.ts) includes MariaDB, WP-CLI, theme installation, and PHP assertions. Vite needs a build, Rust needs `cargo check`, and Web Components need browser tests; forcing them through one host abstraction would add complexity without shared behavior.

I’d standardize the **contract** instead: each adapter gets a `check:compatibility` command, recorded evidence in the [support registry](scripts/release/target-compatibility.json), and a path-scoped CI check. Keep the WordPress Docker code local for now. When Drupal or another service-backed adapter uses the same container setup, extract only proven common pieces such as process execution, health polling, and cleanup. I’ve recorded that boundary in the plan; no repository files changed.

-# mise — the polyglot toolchain + orchestration layer for pantoken.
-#
-# It pins the JS toolchain AND the native toolchains needed to build and verify generated output,
-# and gives one cross-language task runner. pnpm + vite-plus remain the source of truth for the JS
-# packages; mise sits on top for toolchains and native orchestration.

-[tools]
-node = "24"
-pnpm = "11.9.0"
-# Native toolchains are added as targets come online. Swift powers the v1 native proof; on macOS it
-# is provided by Xcode, and mise can manage it on Linux via the swift backend.

-# Planned: java + gradle (Compose), dart/flutter (Flutter), php + composer (Drupal).
+# mise coordinates native toolchains and checks; Vite+ manages the JS runtime and workspace.

+run = "vp run -r build"

- User priority (2026-09-29): finish web-based adapter verification before returning to iOS runtime work. Do not run simulator/app/asset-catalog checks yet.
- Swift currently has `environment-verified` evidence only: Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4 / iOS Simulator SDK 27.0 typechecked generated UIKit source for arm64 iOS 15 deployment target. This is NOT proof of an iOS 15 runtime floor.
- Return after web adapters: build a disposable iOS app, boot/install/launch on an installed simulator, assert generated token values at runtime, compile and load optional `Icons.xcassets`; document exact simulator/SDK and do not claim older iOS runtimes without testing them.
- During rollout: incremental conventional commits + changesets including private packages, `vp test --coverage` last after test edits; do not run translations. Defer Snyk until all adapters are done.

**Configuration**: [docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts](docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts)
- Defines `LOCALE_THEMES` object per locale (label, lang, description, sidebar structure)
- Each locale has unique `guidePrefix` (e.g., `"/guide/"` for root, `"/<locale>/guide/"` for others)

- **Locale routing math**: `prefix swap` — page at `hu/guide/cli.md` accessed as `/<locale>/guide/cli`
  - Enforced by `check-locale-parity.ts` — all locales have symmetric content parity
  - Search index locale keys via `useData().locale.value`
- **Root locale only mode** (`DOCS_ROOT_LOCALE_ONLY=1`): Skips non-root `/api/` (untranslated API); serves root `/api/` from other locales
  - Used in CI partial builds to save build time/memory (line 379-386 in config.ts)

### Docs Build Orchestration and Validation
**Asset generation**: `docs/scripts/run-assets.ts` — orchestrates 15+ independent generators
- Dependencies tracked explicitly (not shell `&&`):
  - `demos` depends on `site-themes` 
  - `icon-manifest` depends on `cdn-icon-manifest` + `cdn-plugin-manifest`
  - Others run in parallel
- Concurrency: `DOCS_ASSETS_CONCURRENCY` env var (default: machine parallelism)
- Used by CI: Tasks run as part of `vp run @pantoken/docs#build`

- **Generator**: `scripts/release/generate-compatibility.ts` — runs `buildCompatibility()` from `compatibility.ts`
  - Reads: `formats/tokens/generated/meta.json` (provenance), `scripts/release/target-compatibility.json` (curated support claims)
  - Outputs: `compatibility.json` (machine-readable), `docs/compatibility.md` (rendered table)
  - Task: `vp run sync:compatibility` (vite.config.ts line 230-233, depends on `build:all`)
  - Uses: `renderMarkdown(compat: Compatibility): string` to format human-readable tables
- **Gate**: `scripts/release/check-compatibility.ts` — fails if committed `compatibility.json` drifts
  - Task: `vp run gate:compatibility` (vite.config.ts line 234-237, depends on `build:all`)
  - Always runs in CI `ready:all` gate (cheap, only changes on pins or consumer-set edits)
  - Compares parsed JSON, not text (whitespace-tolerant)
- **Current output**: [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md) — generated markdown table with upstream sources + consumer matrix

### Docs Build Validation and Publishing
**Full docs build** (CI workflow): [.github/workflows/docs.yml](workflows/docs.yml)
- Triggered: On docs-only merge to main, package release (via `docs-deploy-request` artifact), or manual dispatch
- Build steps (lines 206-292):
  1. `vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build` — build package deps (includes compatibility generation)
  2. Changed-page detection: `node docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts` (computes diff scope, outputs to temp JSON file)
  3. Either partial build (modified locales only) or full build (fallback if no cache or full_build flag)
  4. `docs:build:deploy` or `docs:build:deploy:partial` VitePress task
  5. Upload build timings artifact

  - `DOCS_BUILD_LOCALE_CONCURRENCY: "2"` — max parallel locale builds (4-core runner limit)
- Deployment: `docs/scripts/prepare-cloudflare-deploy.ts` prepares tree, then `wrangler deploy` to Cloudflare Workers

- Locale mirrors: `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts` copies `.md` + translates via adapter

  - `i18n.config.json` specifies `docs.guides.pot` from `docs/guide/**/*.md` pattern (does not include root)
  - To add to extraction, must register in `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts` or extend i18n config glob
- Drift check: `vp run gate:i18n` — ensures locale PO files kept current (fails if new strings added to English)

### Release Link Conventions
**URLs**:
- **Absolute root-relative**: All public assets use `/path.json` format (no domain, works across all locales)
- **Canonical URL builder**: `canonicalUrl(relativePath): string` (config.ts line 550-552)
  - Template: `${hostname}${relativePath}` with `.md` stripped
  - Example: `https://pantoken.app/guide/getting-started` (for both root and locale routes via symmetric prefix swap)
- **Multilocale alternate links** (hreflang for SEO):
  - Built by `alternateLinks()` func (config.ts line 575-597)
  - Each page carries hreflang links for every locale + `x-default`
  - Links computed via prefix swap from current page's relative path

### Changed-Page Detection for Partial Builds
**Script**: [docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts](docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts)
- Computes which `.md` files changed vs. base ref (default: `origin/main`)
- Resolves dependencies: A component API change → rebuild all locale API mirrors for that component
- Outputs: JSON file (path via `DOCS_CHANGED_PAGES_FILE` env) + GitHub outputs
- Used by CI: If partial build succeeds, faster than full rebuild; fallback to full if changed-page resolution fails
- **Scope limitation**: Cannot handle metadata-only changes (e.g., only `compatibility.json` changed, no `.md` touched)
  - Implication: compatibility registry changes should be paired with any `.md` update, or full rebuild forced
